subject: Lumenix private inference VPC — sudden throughput drop, p95 spike and 500s (urgent)
messages:
From: Amit Shah <amit@lumenix.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@lumenix.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production alert: private cluster throughput dropping, p95 latency rising

Hi Stephanie —

We've been seeing a sustained throughput decline on our private VPC deployment since ~02:00 PT this morning. Key symptoms:
- P95 generation latency jumped from ~320ms to ~2.1s across the board.
- Intermittent 500 responses from the inference gateway; about 1.2% of requests in the last hour.
- Overall throughput down ~35% compared to yesterday baseline.

This is across all zones in our VPC, and we haven't rolled any app-level changes. We did push a maintenance kernel/security patch to the host OS Friday night but the timing doesn't line up perfectly. Can you triage immediately? Our SLAs are impacted and we're getting escalation from the platform team and CTO.

Attached: recent logs + sampling of failing request traces.
[Attachment: lumenix_logs.zip (compressed logs, 28MB)]

What we need: immediate remediation plan, ETA for rollback/fallback, and a runbook we can use to reduce customer impact. If useful, loop in anyone from your infra/serving runtime team.

Thanks —
Amit
Amit Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, Lumenix
amit@lumenix.ai

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@lumenix.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production alert: private cluster throughput dropping, p95 latency rising

Amit — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We're on it.

Immediate plan (first 30 minutes):
- Marcus will run a lightweight telemetry sweep to identify whether the p95 jump correlates with KV cache misses or a backend decode stall.
- Laura will review recent autoscaling events and reserved pool metrics for the tenant.
- Irene will validate the inference runtime kernel/quantization mismatch possibilities and check recent kernel updates.

Please confirm whether you want us to open a temporary read-only maintenance window (5–10m) for deeper probes. Also confirm whether the private deployment is on the latest Redwood runtime (v1.14.2) and whether you applied any recent operator-level changes.

We'll send a short exec-friendly summary within 60 minutes and a remediation recommendation shortly after.

-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production alert: private cluster throughput dropping, p95 latency rising

Stephanie / team — quick notes from the initial sweep:
- KV cache hit rate on the Lumenix tenant fell from ~91% to ~46% starting at 01:55 PT (matches their symptom window). That explains a lot of the token-level p95 increase.
- Several worker nodes are showing heavy GC/CPU contention in the logs Amit attached; suspect a config drift where the in-proc batching worker counts were lowered by the node operator agent during the host patch.
- Error 500 traces are originating at the model scorer process, often following a long tail decode (50–200ms extra) that pushes through and triggers a gateway timeout under the client's client-side deadline.

Short remediation proposal:
1) Push a temporary config override to bump in-proc batching concurrency + reinstate the prior worker count.
2) Increase the KV cache allocation for the tenant (hot key eviction threshold adjustment).
3) If 1–2 don't recover p95 within 15–20m, deploy the rc_fallback_runbook.pdf plan (fallback model variant with smaller context & quantized weights) to reduce per-token latency and lower error amplification.

I attached the draft runbook for the fallback deploy and a minimal rollback patch we can apply if needed. I'll start step (1) now and monitor.

[Attachment: rc_fallback_runbook.pdf]
[Attachment: rollback.patch]

-marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@lumenix.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: Amit Shah <amit@lumenix.ai>, procurement@lumenix.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 10:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production alert: private cluster throughput dropping, p95 latency rising

Stephanie / Marcus —

We appreciate the prompt attention. This incident is visible to our execs; the CTO is asking for a timeline and whether we should expect a customer-facing outage. Please note: we have a high-volume batch expected at 14:00 PT that could be impacted. If a fallback model reduces quality below our SLO for customer-facing features we will need a documented mitigation and an ask for temporary credit for the affected window.

Please include an ETA for the fallback deploy and any expected change in inference quality metrics.

—Elena
Elena Rossi
CTO, Lumenix
elena.rossi@lumenix.ai

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec brief: Lumenix private VPC incident — recommended actions and asks

Team — sending a concise internal exec note to align approvals and any commercial/credits asks. Please review; I will forward to Sales Leadership and Finance if we agree.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause (working hypothesis): post-host patch config drift + reduced in-proc worker counts => KV cache eviction pressure => increased downstream decode latency and gateway timeouts.
- Impact: p95 latency ~2.1s, errors ~1.2%, throughput -35%. Customer-facing batch at 14:00 PT at risk.

Recommended immediate actions (we can execute within 15–30m):
A) Apply Marcus' config override (in-proc worker counts + concurrency). Estimated recovery window: 10–20m.
B) Adjust tenant KV cache allocation (non-disruptive config bump). Recovery window: 5–15m after change.
C) Prepare & stand by to deploy rc_fallback_runbook.pdf (fallback model) if A+B don't restore p95 — estimated deployment time 22–30m, with rollback.patch available for immediate revert.

Commercial / exec asks:
- Approve a temporary credits offer for Lumenix covering up to 4 hours of degraded quality if we deploy fallback (requested by Lumenix execs).
- Approve priority engineering bandwidth (Marcus + 2 infra) until incident stabilized (estimate 4h).

Related links: HubSpot deal LD-8421, incident docs on shared drive.

If approved, I will notify Lumenix with ETA and the fallback quality tradeoffs (expected drop in answer-length and slight token-level quality variance due to quantized variant).

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@lumenix.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@lumenix.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Lumenix incident update & agreed action plan (ETA + mitigations)

Amit / Elena —

Quick update and plan following the investigation:
- What we did: applied an in-proc worker count override and increased tenant KV cache allocation at 09:45 PT; monitored for 45m. Initial recovery: p95 improved to ~520ms and throughput recovered ~28% within 30m of the changes.
- Fallback: we held on deploying the fallback model; it is ready (rc_fallback_runbook.pdf) and will be deployed at your approval if we see another regression before the 14:00 batch. The rollback.patch is available for immediate revert of the fallback.
- Quality impact: fallback will reduce response length and use a quantized variant — expected small drop in generation diversity; we have baseline evals ready to share.

Executive asks we discussed:
- Redwood is prepared to offer up to 4 hours of service credit for workload periods demonstrably impacted if the fallback is deployed. Laura, please coordinate with Finance on the concrete credit number.
- We recommend activating the priority engineering window for Lumenix for the next 6 hours (Marcus + 2).

Next steps:
1) Lumenix to confirm whether to proceed with fallback pre-batch (we will hold ~20m for your sign-off).
2) If yes, we will schedule a 22–30m deploy starting on approval and share a post-deploy quality snapshot.
3) If no, we will keep the config overrides live and monitor for 24h; we'll schedule an after-action call tomorrow morning.

Attachments: rc_fallback_runbook.pdf, rollback.patch
[Attachment: rc_fallback_runbook.pdf]
[Attachment: rollback.patch]

Thanks —
-Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
